hypothesis: Combine the no-full-tile padded accumulator with streamed column compaction. A map callback, driven by the existing Nt-length weight descriptor, copies each physical column through the Mt-halfword temporary using explicit bank1 DSRs. This tests whether limiting packing-code expansion leaves more program-memory budget than a static-bound loop. Extra weight reads remain inside timing; no requested work or layout conversion is omitted.
falsification: Reject wrong map invocation count, descriptor/map-state clobber, unread-column overwrite, missing K/N work or communication, FP16/ABI/timing/PE change, fixed numerical or shutdown failure, memory above1.10x, speedup below1.05x or failed fresh six-case pairing. Compare both packing implementations and the qualified full-tile incumbent; code-size reduction alone is not retention.
